title: Messenger
tagline: Two phones, a server and a push gateway: follow one message from the clock icon to the two blue ticks.

tour.title: Five actors, one wire
tour.text: Two phones, a server, a push gateway and a network module that carries every packet. Structure shows the pieces and the layers: nothing in the actors layer may reach upward, and the actors never call each other.

tour.title: Where things run
tour.text: Alice sends a message and little packets cross the wire. Deployment shows what the code alone does not say: each actor is its own process on its own machine, and everything between them travels through the network.

tour.title: One message, five states
tour.text: Bob opens the chat and the two grey ticks turn blue. The ticks are drawn from this state machine: composing, queued, sent, delivered, read. It can only move forward, one step at a time, so a message is never read before it is delivered.

tour.title: Bob loses Wi-Fi
tour.text: Bob's phone drops from online to offline. A different machine, a different question: what can the phone's link be? It must say hello and be welcomed (syncing) before it sends anything again.

tour.title: The server notices, then nudges
tour.text: Alice writes to an offline Bob. Her message is stored (one grey tick), but the server only learns Bob is gone after five quiet seconds. Only then does it ask the push gateway to nudge his phone: wait a few seconds and watch.

tour.title: The rules behind it
tour.text: Bob comes back, says hello, and the server resends what it was holding. The constraints list what must never happen: the server never lets a message go before its recipient confirms, a message is never shown twice, and push is never used for an online phone.

tour.title: A flaky network
tour.text: Packets start to disappear. The outbox retries with a doubling delay and the server dedupes by message id, so everything still arrives once, in the server's order. Concurrency shows those retry timers and the shared state they touch.

tour.title: What was left out on purpose
tour.text: Roles list what each building block needs: a key for every map, a capacity for every queue, a tie-break for every ordering. Two endpoints say outright that they check nobody's identity: this is a simulation, and the absence is declared, not forgotten.
